minutes.headline: Open Space Committee voted to authorize $500 from the donation fund for a title examination of the Stump Cove parcel.
minutes.summary: The ad hoc Open Space Committee approved its June minutes, discussed vacancies on the committee, and had members introduce themselves. The main business was a roll-call vote to fund a title examination of the town-owned parcel off Reservoir Road for possible Lake Shirley access. The committee also heard parks and conservation updates, set the next meeting for October 20, and adjourned.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the June 9, 2022 meeting by roll call
votes.outcome: passed; all four members voted aye by roll call

votes.motion: Authorize 500 out of the Bright Farms fund to pursue title examination and certification of the Stump Cove parcel, by roll call
votes.outcome: passed; chair said it carries after roll call of four

budget_items.topic: Title examination of Stump Cove parcel
budget_items.what_was_said: A title examiner quoted a price well below the amount the committee had earlier discussed allocating. The cost depends on how hard the search is.
The committee holds a trust fund from a donation to open space that it may spend at its discretion without town meeting. The town manager acts as fiscal agent and does the contracting.
A member suggested authorizing a not-to-exceed amount with a progress report at the cap. Another preferred to authorize only the estimate and revisit after a report.

decisions.decision: Chair will ask the town manager to start the contracting process with town counsel's title examiner, with a report hoped for at the next meeting.
Next meetings: September 8 stands, and the October meeting moved to October 20 at 7:30 p.m. on Zoom.
Mary will follow up with the Conservation Commission chair about a bequest and report at the next meeting.

The chair will ask the town manager to start contracting with town counsel's title examiner, with a report hoped for at the next meeting.
The examiner's quote came in well below the amount the committee had earlier discussed; members split on a not-to-exceed cap versus authorizing only the estimate.
The committee set its next meetings: September 8 stands and the October meeting moves to October 20 on Zoom.
A member will follow up with the Conservation Commission chair about a bequest and report back.

why_it_matters: The parcel is town-owned land off Reservoir Road being checked for possible Lake Shirley access, and the title work is a first step that comes before any decision about using it.
The money comes from a donated trust fund the committee may spend without a town meeting vote, so this spending did not go through a vote residents are asked to take.
